title: Economic factors in growing crops
log: 2026-11-12T12:44:18Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new
2026-11-12T15:15:42Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: The closest bank point, geo-economic-factors-farming, covers land, labour, investment and transport in a Year 9 introduction, but it does not teach prices, trade rules, government support or how these shape a farmer's choice of crop, so it is related rather than the same idea.

draft.title: Economic factors in growing crops
card: Farmers tend to grow crops that they expect to sell at a good price. If the price of a crop falls, some farmers may switch to another crop.
Farmers pay for labour (workers) and inputs such as seed, fertiliser, fuel and water. A crop that needs many workers or costly inputs leaves less profit.
A crop must reach buyers. A farm far from a town, port or good road pays more to move its crop. A crop that spoils fast is hard to grow far from its market.
Trade rules, such as taxes on imports or limits on exports, change what a crop can earn. Government support, such as payments or cheap loans, can make a crop worth growing.
draft.remember: Farmers choose crops by what they can earn after costs, and whether the crop can reach buyers.

a.q: The price of cotton falls, while the price of chickpeas rises. What is a farmer most likely to do?
opts: Grow more chickpeas and less cotton
Grow more cotton and less chickpeas
Keep both crops because prices do not matter
Stop farming because chickpeas cost more
a.why: Farmers tend to grow crops they expect to sell at a good price, so a higher chickpea price makes chickpeas more attractive. Growing more of the cheaper crop would cut the farmer's likely earnings.
a.clue: Which crop is now likely to earn more?

b.q: Ravi farms in a remote valley with no sealed road to a town. Which crop is he least likely to choose?
opts: Fresh strawberries that spoil within days
Dried beans that keep for many months
Wheat that can be stored in a silo
Oats that can be stored for a long time
b.why: Poor transport makes it costly and slow to reach buyers, and strawberries spoil fast. The other three crops keep well, so a slow trip to market matters much less.
b.clue: Think about which crop cannot wait for a slow trip to market.

a.best: Grow more chickpeas and less cotton

b.best: Fresh strawberries that spoil within days
